evidence.summary: At cycle 205, coolant_pressure_bar dropped to 2.896 bar (-4.4%, z=-1.8) and coolant_flow_l_min fell to 38.713 L/min (-2.9%, z=-2.0) compared to baseline, indicating reduced coolant circulation.
SOP-C-201 notes that coolant pressure falling below 2.6 bar and flow below 36 L/min together signal a coolant leak; our values are approaching these thresholds.
SOP-C-202 describes filter differential pressure >0.7 bar for filter clog; observed dp is 0.412 bar, not indicative of clog.
RUL estimate for unit U052 is 87 cycles remaining, policy band above_50_monitor, suggesting the unit is still healthy but warrants monitoring.
Similar unit U007 experienced a coolant leak (ticket T1006) with low flow alarm and pressure around 3.0 bar, resolved by replacing a seal.

report.summary: Unit U052 showed a moderate anomaly (score 0.566) driven by decreased coolant pressure (2.896 bar) and flow (38.7 L/min) relative to baseline. These deviations approach the thresholds defined in SOP-C-201 for coolant leaks, though they have not yet crossed the critical limits (2.6 bar, 36 L/min). Filter differential pressure remains low, ruling out filter clog per SOP-C-202. No bearing wear or sensor fault signatures are present. RUL remains healthy (87 cycles). Based on similar past incident (T1006) and current sensor trends, the likely root cause is an early-stage coolant leak. Recommend a targeted inspection of the coolant circuit and fittings, and replace any compromised seals.
